label: Stake-First List
line: The stake first, then the question and the count, then three items with one concrete tool or number each, the least expected one last.
best_for: practical advice or a set of checks
the separate reasons one thing is fast, safe or cheap
also_for: the causes of one problem, when they do not form a chain
avoid_for: items that form a sequence: that is a flow
a list whose every item must be covered when there are more than four: the formula keeps the three or four strongest
a list with no stake: nothing makes the viewer need it
signals: the topic is a set of separate items
a pain or a figure makes the list worth having
each item has one concrete tool, number or example
one item is less expected than the rest

beats.name: Stake
beats.job: The pain or the figure that makes the list necessary.

beats.name: Question and count
beats.job: How to reverse it, and how many things there are. Say the last one is the odd one.

beats.name: Items
beats.job: One vivid name and one concrete tool or number each, the least expected last.

beats.name: The odd one, explained
beats.job: Why the last item holds. Stop there.

hooks.shape: You will not [goal] while [pain]. So how do you [reverse it]? There are three things.
[N] things make [X] [quality]. The last one sounds wrong.
Why is [X] so [quality] when [similar thing] is not?

holds: The stake makes the list worth sitting through, the count tells the viewer how far along they are, and the promise about the last item holds them to the end.
ending: The last item and why it holds, then stop.
first_frame: The stake as a picture or a number, beside a numbered row whose last slot is a question mark.
pitfalls: The bare list label as the opening
Items of equal weight with nothing saved for last
A summary or an ask after the last item
An item with no tool, number or example
template: [Pain or figure]. So how do you [reverse it]? There are three things. One: [vivid name]. [Concrete tool or number]. Two: [vivid name]. [Concrete]. And the odd one: [vivid name]. [Concrete]. It sounds wrong, but [why it holds].
